engagement_title: Girdermark Components data-sheet library: rebuild the printer's spec sheet and the label house's bin label into two live merges, recover the house mark off a cast nameplate, and ship the whole active range as sheets, labels and a portal front page
vertical: Manufacturing and Industrial, OEM elevator and electrical replacement components sold to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors through a new dealer portal and a trade counter (Cleveland, Ohio)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork brief posted by a B2B wholesale distributor of electrical and elevator replacement parts selling to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors, who wanted distributor-facing product material with clean product photography and complete specs and pricing for every part. Laundered to the fictional Girdermark Elevator and Electrical Supply and its components division; no real company, person, product or trademark appears (the earlier 'Ironclad' laundering was dropped because the bare word collides with an unrelated real firm). Co-anchor: the Upwork packaging brief from a construction-chemicals maker wanting its legacy product-label PDFs rebuilt into an editable, maintainable Adobe layout system, quoting '49 products, many with 1-3 variants', 'different bottle and canister sizes', 'recreate the labels based on the existing design (no new design required)', with 'updated texts, product images, barcodes' supplied and the deliverable required to be 'editable, print-ready files (CMYK, with bleed)'. The ledger records this slot as previously repositioned down to a single per-part sheet run, which is one surface and one deliverable class. LAYOUT-27 restores the commission both clients actually posted: two different flat PDFs owned by two different vendors have to become two live templates driven off one reconciled roster, the client's own mark has to be recovered before either template can carry it, and the pictures have to be fixed because they are what the sheet and the label both show.
client_one_liner: Sixteen active parts, a spec sheet and a bin label we only own as the printer's PDFs, a company mark nobody has the artwork for, and a dealer portal that goes live in five weeks.
client_brief:
Girdermark Components, dealer portal and warehouse relabel.

We are the components division. Sixteen parts are active this season and every one of them needs a data sheet on the new dealer portal and a bin label on the mezzanine racking, which is being installed in five weeks.

Here is our problem. We do not own any of our own artwork. Our spec sheet is printed for us and all we have is the file the printer sends back. Same story for the bin label: the label house designed it, we get a PDF. Both look right and both are what our dealers and our pickers already recognise, so keep them exactly as they are and put this season's parts through them. The specs, the ordering codes and the prices come out of our stock system and I am attaching that export. Those values are what a customer holds us to, so nothing gets reworded or shortened to make it fit. If something will not fit, I want to hear it from you before it prints, not from a picker.

Our mark is the other problem. The artwork was lost in an office move years ago. The only two places it still exists are the header of the printed sheet and the cast plate riveted to the old traction machine in the back, which I have photographed for you. We need it back as real artwork we can use anywhere, because it goes on every sheet and every label and right now somebody scans it off a page every time.

Our part photography also needs pulling together. It was shot on the bench over several months and the bench mat got replaced part way through, so the backgrounds do not match and neither does the light. Every sheet carries a picture and every label carries a small one, and they have to look like one range.

Finally the portal needs a front page: what the range is, how to order, and one place where our mark and our type are written down so the next person does not scan anything off a page again. Send that back as something we can edit ourselves.

Parts run 400 to 9,000 dollars and our buyers have been specifying this class of part for twenty years. Flat and accurate. No styling.
price_band_and_audience: Components from 400 dollars (relay sockets, restrictor brackets, contactor blocks) to 9,000 dollars (governor sheave assemblies, door operator arm assemblies). The buyer is 35 to 60, a working service technician, a building maintenance supervisor or an electrical contractor who judges a supplier by whether the photograph and the spec table agree. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this tier the sheet is flat, even and technical: one neutral ground, the whole part in frame, generous spec setting, prices plain in the run of the page, no atmosphere. Push it toward bright consumer-tool photography with warm light and shallow depth and the buyer reads a 15 dollar hardware brand and stops trusting the load ratings printed beside it. Push it the other way into dark cinematic hero work and it reads as marketing rather than a parts catalogue. The bin label answers to a different reader again: a picker at arm's length under warehouse light, so it is bigger, blunter and carries less. A posted job of this shape runs 2,200 to 4,000 dollars fixed, or 45 to 75 dollars an hour across 40 to 60 hours.

brand_identity.sector: A B2B distributor of OEM elevator and electrical replacement components, sold to service technicians, maintenance supervisors and electrical contractors.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: The components division of Girdermark Elevator and Electrical Supply, based in Cleveland, Ohio, supplying through a trade counter and a new dealer portal.

The whole proposition is that the photograph and the spec table agree, every time, so a buyer can specify to the exact value and trust the load rating printed beside it. It sells accuracy, not atmosphere.
brand_identity.audience: Working buyers aged thirty five to sixty who have specified this class of part for twenty years and judge a supplier by whether the picture and the numbers match.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Parts from 400 to 9,000 dollars. A flat, even, technical register: one neutral photographic ground, the whole part in frame, generous spec setting, prices plain in the run of the page. Never bright consumer tool styling and never dark cinematic hero work. The bin label answers to a picker at arm's length, so it is bigger, blunter and carries less.
brand_identity.typography: A technical, legible system: a neutral grotesque sans for part numbers, spec tables and labels where clarity at small size and at arm's length is everything, with a plain companion for running copy. No decorative or humanist warmth. Note that no chosen face can reach the printer's sheet or the label house's label, which keep their existing typography.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt, factual and useful. No marketing adjectives, no styling in the words. Example line the brand would write: "Sixteen active parts this season. Specs, codes and prices are exactly as our system holds them."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The division owns none of its own artwork. The spec sheet and the bin label exist only as the flat press PDFs the printer and the label house return. The house mark was lost in an office move and survives only in the printed sheet header and cast into an aluminium nameplate riveted to an old traction machine in the back, photographed for reference. Part photography was shot in house on the bench over several months and does not match.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy above all: the picture and the spec must agree, values are never reworded to fit, and anything that will not fit is raised before it prints.

assets_supplied.name: sheet_2026_PRESS.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the current per-part data sheet, US Letter portrait, one part per page, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a header block with the house mark, a two-column spec table, a part photograph, a certification strip and an ordering-code panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sends back to us each season. We have never had the working file. Keep it exactly as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed page sets the spec table as rows reading across two columns, but the file's own content order runs all the way down the left visual column and then all the way down the right, and the ordering-code panel that reads as a separate box belongs to the same continuous story, so the order a human reads off the printed page and the order the story actually holds do not agree at any point past the first row. The two graphic frames, the part photograph and the certification strip, are separable only by their bounds and their existing link, and neither is named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: label_2026_PRESS.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The label house's flat press PDF of the bin label, 100 x 62 mm, one label per page, fonts embedded. Carries the house mark, the part number set large, a description line, the ordering code and a small part picture.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label house designed this for us. It is what the pickers know. Same instruction: keep it, just put this season through it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The description sits in a fixed-measure frame sized to last season's longest string. It does not spill, it does not warn and it does not report anything: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a longer record is cut off mid-word on a label that otherwise renders perfectly at trim. Separately, the die outline is a placed graphic rather than a document bleed, so nothing in the file carries real bleed and none can be introduced into it.

assets_supplied.name: range_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the components stock system, one row per active part, with part number, description, spec parameters, ordering code, list and dealer price, a finish column and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system. Those values are ours and they are what the customer holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The spec columns sit in the stock system's own order, which is not the order the printed sheet prints them in, and three values the sheet carries (certification code, seismic rating, superseded-by code) are not columns at all but are packed into one semicolon-delimited attributes blob. Finishes are internal two-letter codes rather than names, the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, and two of the rows are revision variants of one part number that the system still emits side by side.

assets_supplied.name: nameplate/ (4 frames, 4200 x 2800)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone and camera frames of the cast aluminium nameplate riveted to the traction machine in the back of the warehouse, shot at different angles under a shop droplight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark still physically exists apart from the printed sheet. Shot it four ways because I did not know what you would need."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is raised casting in the same aluminium as the plate, so it reads by shadow rather than by colour and a selection that names the plate returns the plate. Its keyline is a hairline rule and its letterforms carry tight enclosed counters, and a trace that looks immaculate at the size it is traced at does not necessarily hold at the size the mark is actually reproduced at on a bin label, on the amber label stock, once the render comes back at trim.

assets_supplied.name: bench_photos/ (16 frames, 4800 x 3200)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house part photography of the sixteen active components, shot on the bench in the back of the warehouse across several months under shop fluorescents.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same bench, same camera, different days. The backgrounds do not match and neither does the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bench mat was replaced part way through the shoot, so eight frames sit on a mid grey and eight on a near black, which shifted both the exposure the camera chose and the apparent value of every plated part, in the same direction on every affected frame. Four of the components (the sheave, the restrictor bracket, the cable clamp and the operator arm) enclose through-bores and open frames that a one-call knockout fills with captured mat while reporting complete success.

acceptance_bar: All sixteen parts read as one range: one neutral, one white point, one black point, judged with the pictures laid out together rather than one at a time.
Every part picture shows the whole part at a consistent subject scale, both at sheet size and at label size. A sharp, well composed picture of one end of a part is a rejected picture.
Through-bores and open frames are genuinely open in the sheet cutouts, not filled with captured bench mat.
No delivered file is larger on either axis than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture any tool resized and by how much.

The recovered mark is delivered as real placeable artwork: scalable, transparent, with no background plate riding along, and it holds at both the size it prints on the sheet header and the size it prints on the bin label, on the actual label ground.

Data sheets: exactly one page per current part, every field the printed sheet carries present on every page, every value bound verbatim from our export and paired with the parameter it actually belongs to.
The photograph on each sheet is the part named on that sheet, and it is in the photograph's frame rather than the certification strip's frame.
Bin labels: one label per current part at 100 x 62 mm trim, every description reaching its end on the label rather than stopping at a frame edge.
Nothing in the export may be reworded, abbreviated or shortened to make it fit. Anything that will not fit as the layout stands is escalated in writing before either file goes to a printer.
The press files render at real print resolution at true trim, and there is one named single file per part for each of the two runs, each containing the part its name claims.
The portal front page comes back as one working file we can edit ourselves, with live text, our recovered mark as real artwork and one named type system.

A written note: what was done to each picture, how the mark was recovered and what it can and cannot be used at, every value in our export that was questioned and what was decided, every field the two templates could not carry, and the fact that neither supplied layout can be given bleed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: Sheets and labels are record per page against layouts the client owns and has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The portal front page does not exist yet and must stay editable, so it belongs on HTML authoring. The mark has to exist as artwork before either template can carry it, which puts imaging first rather than last.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, with the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the two press PDFs, the stock export, the four nameplate frames and the sixteen bench frames, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Two templates, two runs and sixteen parts means the mapping between URL, part and role has to survive forty artefacts.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by part and role.

trajectory.action: Preview the four nameplate frames and pick one, judging squareness, evenness and how hard the droplight is raking across the casting.
trajectory.judgement: A raised casting reads by shadow, so the frame with the strongest raking light gives the most legible lettering and the worst geometry, and the squarest frame gives the flattest, weakest lettering. That trade decides everything downstream and it is made by looking.
trajectory.produces: A chosen nameplate frame with the reason recorded.

trajectory.action: Level the chosen frame, then select the lettering itself by naming its own visual properties rather than naming the plate it is cast into.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate and returns a plate-shaped blob that every downstream step accepts. Naming colour, medium and form pulls it to the raised strokes.
trajectory.produces: A lettering-level mask of the mark with the prompt wording recorded.

trajectory.action: Invert, fill to a flat ground, crop to the mark's own bounds, trace it, then repair the trace: inject a viewBox and strip the opaque full-canvas path so it can sit on a coloured ground.
trajectory.judgement: A trace that returns successfully is not yet a placeable mark. The two repairs are not performed by any tool and nothing warns if they are skipped.
trajectory.produces: A repaired scalable transparent SVG of the mark at trace scale, with the route recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview all sixteen bench frames and triage: which mat, how the exposure ran, how level, and which parts enclose voids.
trajectory.judgement: The client says same bench and same camera. Half the range disagrees, in one consistent direction. The parts that enclose voids have to be identified before any isolation route is chosen, not after.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering mat, exposure, level and part geometry.

trajectory.action: Level what needs levelling, fix one neutral from the better-lit half, and correct each frame toward it with its own parameter set.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across sixteen frames rather than sixteen locally pleasing pictures. A single batched call applies one identical parameter set and ships half the range on the wrong ground value.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen corrected masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Isolate each part onto the sheet ground, routing per part: coherent solid bodies through the one-call knockout, bored and open-framed parts through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the ground.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout fills an enclosed bore with captured mat and reports success, and a sheave with a filled bore is a part the buyer does not recognise. The route is a per-part decision made by looking at the part.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen ground-isolated parts with the route recorded per part.

trajectory.action: Derive the sheet picture and the much smaller label picture for every part, reading each crop's reported detection confidence and tradeoffs rather than trusting the success line, then lay both sets out together.
trajectory.judgement: Subject scale across a set is a set-level decision that cannot be taken one picture at a time, and the label picture is small enough that a crop which reads fine at sheet size can be unreadable at label size.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen sheet pictures and sixteen label pictures with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the export against the printed sheet, the printed label and the pictures: unpack the attributes blob into real fields, expand the finish codes, resolve the two revision rows, compose the description field both templates will carry, and shape the image column into the form the merge contract requires with bare filenames in the cells.
trajectory.judgement: The composed description is the agent's own authorship, it is what both runs print, and how much is packed into it is a decision taken now that is expensive to revisit later. The revision pair is the client's call to make, not the agent's, and the difference has to be said out loud.
trajectory.produces: The reconciled merge data file, uploaded picture masters, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the sheet PDF to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, read the true frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and reconstruct the true story text by concatenating the content runs. Then lay that reconstructed order against the printed page, line by line.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the printer's system happened to emit, not by what the plan assumed. Two graphic frames come back separable only by bounds and link, and deciding which one holds the photograph rather than the certification strip is a judgement made against the printed reference.
trajectory.produces: The converted sheet document, its IDML, a real frame inventory, and the reconstructed story with its order compared against the printed page.

trajectory.action: Author the sheet mapping covering every spec parameter, the ordering code, both prices and the photograph, ordering any rows that share a frame against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Offsets have to be computed against a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and rows sharing a frame have to be ordered so their positions still hold against the untouched text.
trajectory.produces: A validated sheet mapping covering the text fields and the correct image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the sheet merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Nothing instructs this check and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before any page exists.
trajectory.produces: A sheet merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge the sheets to a native document with the per-part photographs bound, render the press file and the 300 ppi proofs, and produce per-part named single sheets, identity verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever was asked for, and merging straight to a flat press file forfeits the per-record branch, so the route is chosen rather than defaulted. Naming sixteen files by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer.
trajectory.produces: The sheet press file, 300 ppi proofs and sixteen identity-verified named sheets.

trajectory.action: Run the same archaeology on the bin label PDF: convert, export IDML, reconstruct the story, author and validate the mapping, prepare, verify the placeholders, merge and render the labels at true 100 x 62 mm trim with the mark and the small picture in place.
trajectory.judgement: Nothing learned from the sheet transfers. The label came from a different vendor's system and its granularity, its frame inventory and its story order are its own, so the second template is a second investigation rather than a repeat of the first.
trajectory.produces: The label merge template, the label press file and rendered labels at trim.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered sheet and every rendered label against the export and against the two printed references, at true trim rather than at proof scale, field by field and picture by picture.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the artefact rather than the log. A value paired with the wrong parameter, a description that stops early, and a picture sitting in the certification strip's frame all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A page-by-page and label-by-label reconciliation against the export.

trajectory.action: License one racking or service-context frame with short generic queries, filter to photography, exclude generative results, download at full resolution and grade it into the range neutral. Then ask for type recommendations once per role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to be flat and plausible rather than dramatic. The type pairing is the agent's own because the recommender refuses to pair, numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One licensed graded context frame and one kit with family, foundry or designer and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with two canvas roots (the portal front page and the mark sheet), the range as a real table, the recovered mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper on both a light and a dark ground, every photograph carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and the second through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, so the export is unverified until it is inspected, and the visual channel shows the first canvas only. How much of the front page is table and how much is picture, and whether it leads with the range or the ordering promise, is the actual design work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with both canvases, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the corrected range, the recovered mark and the licensed frame, staying inside the placement cap and re-sending only the entries reported as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What gets escalated versus what gets fixed quietly. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild both templates from the same two PDFs without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name what will not fit and what cannot be given bleed before a printer sees anything.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sheet actually is once it stops being a printed page. The page presents a tidy two-column spec table whose rows plainly read across, plus an ordering-code panel that plainly sits in its own box. What the conversion exposes is a continuous story that runs the whole left visual column and then the whole right one, with the ordering-code panel inside the same story, so from the second row onward the order a person reads off the printed page and the order the document actually holds diverge and never re-converge. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export and read the runs. A mapping authored against the printed page's reading order validates cleanly, prepares successfully and produces pages that are perfectly typeset with every value present and every value attached to the wrong parameter label.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering and no amount of care changes what the conversion returns, and the page gives no signal at all: it looks like the most ordinary two-column table in the world. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says keep the sheet exactly as it is and put this season's parts through it, and mentions no frames, stories or orders; the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that a value be paired with the parameter it belongs to, which is what any client would ask for. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy itself changes: from per-block field mapping to ordered offsets inside one interleaved story, with the ordering-code panel folded in and same-frame rows re-sequenced.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping against the reconstructed story rather than the printed page, re-sequence the rows sharing that frame so their positions hold against the untouched text, re-validate, re-prepare, and confirm the placeholders by round-tripping the template before any page is merged. Then settle which of the two graphic frames is the photograph well by rendering one page and reading it against the printed reference, rather than assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixteen data sheets on a dealer portal on which the bore diameter is printed against the duty rating, the seismic rating against the certification code, and so on down every page, all correctly typeset, all bound verbatim from the client's own export, sold to technicians who order to those exact values from a supplier whose entire pitch is that the picture and the numbers agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives its real reproduction size. Traced off the nameplate it is immaculate: the keyline is crisp, the counters are open, it sits cleanly on white at the size it was traced at, and it looks right in the sheet header. On the bin label it prints about fourteen millimetres wide on amber stock, and only when the label comes back rendered at true trim does it become visible that the hairline keyline has thinned to nothing in places and the tight counters have filled in, so the mark reads as a dark lozenge at picking distance. Nothing measured this, nothing warned, and every prior artefact was genuinely correct at the size it was made at. Which parts of the mark close, and at what point, are properties of this particular casting under this particular droplight and cannot be predicted from the frames or from the trace.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The trace can only be judged at its reproduction size on its real ground, which does not exist until a template has been built and a label rendered at trim, and up to that moment every check the agent can run passes. Tracing more carefully does not help, because the failure is a reduction failure rather than a tracing failure. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark goes on every sheet and every label and asks for it back as real artwork; it asks no question about size, sets no minimum, and names no risk. No earlier step claims the mark was verified small, because no earlier step had anything to look at. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a new piece of artwork. A second cut of the mark has to be derived for small reproduction, which means re-taking the trace from a different route or re-authoring the keyline as drawn vector rather than traced ink, and then deciding whether the sheet and the label may legitimately carry different cuts of one mark at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Go back to the imaging surface and derive a small-size cut: re-select the lettering with a different prompt on a different nameplate frame, or produce the plate as a filled colour version rather than a two-value trace, and rebuild the keyline as authored vector at a weight that holds. Re-repair the SVG (viewBox and background path) for the new cut, decide and document which cut is used where, re-bind it into the label template and re-render at trim to look again. The portal mark sheet then has to carry both cuts and say where each is used, which is a change to a deliverable that was already authored.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Every bin label on a brand new mezzanine racking system carrying a dark blob where the company mark should be, printed once for the whole active range, discovered by the operations manager at arm's length in warehouse light on the day the racking is signed off.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which records the bin label physically cannot hold. The description frame is a fixed measure sized to last season's longest string, and it neither spills nor reports: it stops rendering at the frame edge. The merge reports success, the render reports success, the placeholder verification passed, and the label comes back looking completely normal, with a description that simply ends. Which records are affected depends on the description field the agent itself composed in the data-preparation step out of the export's description, its expanded finish name and its revision marker, so it cannot be read off the roster in advance and it is different for a different composition decision. At proof scale on screen a truncated line and a short line are indistinguishable; the only way to know is to read every rendered label at trim against the roster row it came from.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and neither can care: the overflow is a silent geometric fact of a frame the agent did not draw and cannot redraw, and no tool in the chain surfaces overset. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says nothing is reworded or shortened to fit and that anything that will not fit must be escalated before it prints, which is the client's standing instruction rather than a warning, and no asset description names a frame width or a longest string. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a composition decision taken again for the whole roster: what the description field is made of, whether the finish name and revision marker belong on the label at all, whether the policy changes for every part or only the offenders (which would leave the rack inconsistent), and what has to be escalated because the client has forbidden shortening. The sheet run carries the same composed field, so changing it changes both runs.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-compose the label description field across the whole roster, re-merge and re-render both runs because the sheet carries the same field, then re-read every label at trim rather than assuming the second pass took. Where a description still cannot fit without shortening, escalate it in writing with the exact records named and an alternative offered (a shorter house description supplied by the client, or that part running a second line), rather than trimming it quietly.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Bin labels going onto the racking with descriptions cut off mid-word on the longest and most easily confused parts, on a rack where the description is what the picker reads, from a client who asked in writing to be told before it printed.

deliverables.name: Girdermark Components range photography at one neutral
deliverables.spec: Sixteen in-house frames shot across two different bench mats brought to one neutral with one white point and one black point, delivered as a sheet picture and a label picture per part at consistent subject scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, one line per frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Ground-isolated part cutouts for the sheet run
deliverables.spec: Sixteen components isolated onto the agreed sheet ground with through-bores and open frames genuinely open rather than filled with captured bench mat, and the isolation route recorded per part because coherent solids and parts that enclose voids cannot be produced the same way. True finish appearance preserved through the isolation, since a buyer specifies a finish from these pictures.

deliverables.name: Recovered Girdermark house mark, artwork system
deliverables.spec: The mark lifted off the cast nameplate at lettering level and delivered as real artwork: a scalable transparent vector with a genuine viewBox and no background plate riding along, in the cuts the work proved were actually needed, with each cut's intended reproduction range stated and each one demonstrated at that size on the ground it prints on. Accompanied by the record of how it was recovered, so the next person does not scan it off a page.

deliverables.name: Data-sheet library: press file, per-part named sheets and proofs
deliverables.spec: US Letter portrait, one page per active part in roster order, page count equal to the current part count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every page binds every spec parameter, the ordering code, both prices and the unpacked attribute values verbatim from the stock export and paired with the parameter each belongs to, plus that part's own photograph in the photograph's frame. Accompanied by one single-page file per part named to the part number and identity-verified by opening it. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Bin label run: press file, per-part named labels and proofs
deliverables.spec: 100 x 62 mm trim, one label per active part, rendered at 300 ppi, each carrying the recovered mark at a cut proved to hold at that size on the label ground, the part number, the composed description reaching its end rather than stopping at a frame edge, the ordering code and the small part picture. Produced from a second, independent reverse-engineering of the label house's flat PDF, handed back as a live template with its own derivation record and an explicit statement that no bleed can be introduced into it.

deliverables.name: Dealer portal front page and mark sheet, plus handover and approval board
deliverables.spec: One native editable document holding two canvas roots: the portal front page with the range as a genuine table, live editable prices and the licensed context frame carried as embedded image data, and the mark sheet carrying the recovered mark as real editable vector on both a light and a dark ground alongside the named type system. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, plus a written handover recording the picture work, the recovery route and its size limits, every export value questioned and its resolution, everything the two templates could not carry, and the bleed constraint, and a persistent approval board carrying the corrected range, the mark and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: The surface split: two record-per-page runs to the merge surface because both layouts are fixed client property, the portal front page to HTML authoring because it must stay editable.
Which nameplate frame to recover the mark from, trading raking light that makes the lettering legible against geometry that makes it square.
Whether to name the plate or the lettering when selecting, where naming the substrate returns a plate-shaped blob that every downstream step accepts.
Whether a trace that returned successfully is a placeable mark, given nothing injects a viewBox or strips the background path for you.
Which half of the bench shoot sets the neutral, knowing the mat change moved the exposure in one consistent direction.
Isolation route per part, where the one-call knockout is right for a solid body and returns a filled bore on a sheave while reporting success.
Subject scale policy across two picture sets at two very different reproduction sizes, decided as a set rather than per part.
What the composed description field is made of, given both runs print it and one of them has a frame that will not spill.
Whether the two revision rows are the agent's call or the client's, and how to say so.
Whether to trust the reading order of the printed page or the order the converted document actually holds.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the part photograph rather than the certification strip.
Whether a success message counts as verification of a prepared template.
Whether one cut of the mark can serve both a sheet header and a fourteen millimetre label, or whether the deliverable is genuinely two cuts.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach either printed template.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns a plausible picture of a data sheet. IDENTITY: the mark is this client's actual mark, cast into a plate on their own machine, and a redrawn approximation is a different company's mark on sixteen labels and a dealer portal. The parts are specific components with specific finishes that a technician orders and installs. SPEC: the client needs one page per active part at US Letter and 300 ppi with every value bound verbatim from their own stock export and paired with the parameter it belongs to, one label per part at 100 x 62 mm trim, thirty-two separately named single-record files each containing the part their filename claims, and no delivered picture larger than its source. None of that is produced or checkable by generation. EDITABILITY: three deliverables are defined by being editable, two live merge templates so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, is this value against the right label, does this description reach its end at trim, does this mark still read at fourteen millimetres. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). Five surfaces, honestly counted: image_vectorize is used but is declared Photoshop-family and is never claimed as an Illustrator surface, and document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are never called because they sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template), one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page-count equal to row-count, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi at trim comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. Both supplied PDFs are real font-embedding press PDFs from a full engine, since thin hand-authored PDFs fail conversion opaquely. GRANULARITY IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING: v3 records that frame granularity from a PDF is not under the agent's control, that a continuous flow can collapse to a single frame, and that placed images split the flow, which is exactly the shape this sheet asset is built to (a continuous spec story plus two placed graphics whose only differentiators are bounds and link). The interleaved-order defect is verify-then-ship: before admission, convert the asset and confirm the reconstructed story order diverges from the printed reading order; if it will not reproduce, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. THE FIXED-FRAME TRUNCATION is a property of the supplied label PDF's frame measure and is confirmed by rendering at trim; no tool in the chain surfaces overset, which is what makes it silent. BLEED is correctly declared impossible: v3 verifies that a PDF-derived template carries zero bleed and that useDocumentBleeds does not introduce it, so the task escalates it rather than promising it, and pdfPreset is never used because its enum is undiscoverable. IMAGE BINDING: per-row binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified; sixteen rows sit inside the documented file limits and the recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with and without backgroundColor, and vectorize are all verified headless; the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background, the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry, the mandatory mask-polarity inversion before tracing, the missing viewBox and the opaque path-zero background are all documented findings, and the mark recovery uses exactly the verified extract-and-repair chain. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with per-root canvas sizes is verified, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport is routed through the text/html upload because the payload passes the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call, and the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint rather than quietly ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, no orientation filter, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
